messages:
IncidentBot: PAGING — GPU prefill OOM spike detected on gpu-cluster-4. 23 container restarts in 10m. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefill-oom

amanda: oncall here, looking now. assigning to ryan for runtime triage.

ryan: grabbing logs from the affected hosts. seeing repeated OOM during prefill step, then container SIGKILL and kube restarts. sample: 
```
[2026-03-17T08:02:14Z] model-server[pid=4211]: prefill: allocating KV cache for seq_len=131072 tokens
[2026-03-17T08:02:14Z] cuda: out of memory when allocating 12.8 GiB (device 0)
[2026-03-17T08:02:14Z] model-server: received SIGKILL: oom-kill
```

priya: thanks. looks like large context windows + aggressive prefetching. quick mitigations I recommend: 1) enable aggressive prefill throttling flag (suppress-prefill) for the affected model group, 2) set model config max_prefill_tokens -> 32768, 3) temporarily route requests >64k tokens to cold-fallback model.

jason: I can push a temporary rate-limit rule at the gateway to cap prefill token budget per-request. deploying rule now: `curl -XPOST https://gateway.internal/rate-limit -d '{"rule":"prefill_tokens>65536 -> 5r/min"}'`

ops-bot: Runbook link pinned: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefill-oom. Suggested play: throttle, reduce max_prefill, cordon noisy nodes, increase hot-pool eviction aggressiveness.

amanda: ryan, please take lead on node cordon/eviction. jason, apply gateway rule. priya, create customer impact list + draft update. I'll coordinate comms.

ryan: cordoning nodes with high OOM counts: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-14 gpu-node-15` and marked for hotpool eviction. Also scaling down prefetchers: `kubectl scale deploy/gpu-prefetcher --replicas=1 --namespace=inference` (was 5 -> 1).

jason: gateway rule applied and propagated to edge nodes. hitting it with smoke: `wrk -t2 -c10 -d10s --prefill-tokens 70000` now returns 429 for large prefill.

support-sre: running query to map customers -> traces. initial results: 
```
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) as failures
FROM traces
WHERE error LIKE '%out of memory%' AND env='prod' AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes'
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY failures DESC
LIMIT 10;
-- results: cust_92 (34), cust_238 (12), cust_apple_integration (5)
```

priya: confirmed. 3 paying customers on dedicated capacity impacted, plus ~120 hosted requests from unpredictable clients. severity: partial outage for heavy-context routes. drafting customer note: "We observed GPU memory exhaustion on inference hosts while processing very large-context prefill requests. We applied throttles and reduced prefill size; service is being monitored."

amanda: thumbs-up on the note. post to status page and send targeted DM to affected customers in support queue. customer-success can you prepare the message?

customer-success: drafting now. will send post once we confirm stabilization window >= 10m.

ryan: additional log detail — some containers show CUDA peer-to-peer alloc failure that precedes the OOM: `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: cannot allocate memory` plus `nvml: memory limit reached`. Suggest we enable nv_peer_disable for hotpool as stopgap. Patching daemonset now.

ops-bot: Patch applied: kube-daemonset/gpu-driver updated with env NV_DISABLE_P2P=true. Rolling restart initiated.

priya: mitigation checklist status: suppress-prefill flag ON for model-large-30b, max_prefill_tokens reduced to 32768, gateway prefill cap active, cordoned 2 noisy nodes, prefetcher scaled down. Monitoring dashboards show token-processing rate down 70% and OOM restarts dropping.

amanda: good. switch to monitoring mode. ryan stay on until we have 20m of stable metrics. priya/supp-sre continue customer mapping. jason keep rate limit in place for 30m.

ryan: 12m into mitigation: container restarts down to 2 in last 10m (was 23). memory headroom recovering on cluster.

support-sre: customer list updated, notifying accounts: cust_92 and cust_238 flagged for follow-up.

customer-success: sent targeted messages to affected customers with the draft note. no critical revenue customers impacted but some latency-sensitive flows degraded.

amanda: marking incident as mitigated. creating follow-up ticket for root cause: investigate KV cache sizing with long-context, add proactive throttles for models with >64k sequence, and add e2e test for prefill-edge-cases.

IncidentBot: STATUS -> mitigated. Monitoring for 40 minutes. Created issue INF-5621 (investigate prefill OOMs & improve throttles).

jason: leaving the temporary gateway rule active until INF-5621 owners confirm a safe rollback path.

ryan: I'll run postmortem trace to find the request patterns that triggered the spike. agenda: reproduce with long prompt + rapid parallel prefill, verify KV cache growth.

amanda: thanks everyone. great rapid coordination. :thumbsup:

customer-success: will follow up with customers and update the status page when cleared. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ops-bot: Incident channel will be archived after final postmortem.

amanda: closing thread here; leaving notes for postmortem doc. last check: metrics stable for 18m.
